note: No reason. A prune leaves nothing of what it removed, so the reason recorded at the time is the only account of intent there will ever be; it is REQUIRED rather than encouraged.
No kinds. A prune says what it removes; an empty request that removed whatever the host thought eligible would be a destructive act nobody specified.

A kind outside the two. `expired` is the plausible wrong guess: a record's `validUntil` is sealed, and a host cannot see it, so expiry is never a host's to prune by — a curator retracts expired records and the tombstones age out.

Naming the records to remove. A prune removes what the room's stated retention makes eligible, which every member could read in advance; removing records an administrator picks by key is a different act, and not one this task performs.

An override of the retention carried in the request. Eligibility is decided by the retention in force, which members can read; a prune carrying its own would remove records under a rule nobody was shown. Change the retention first, with rooms/records/retention/set.
`dryRun: false` on a real prune. Absent is how a real prune is spelled; two spellings of one meaning are two things for readers to disagree about.
A response that does not say which retention decided eligibility. A caller holding an earlier listing checks every disappearance against it; without it the removal cannot be checked by anybody.
0.1's `prune.at` does not exist in 0.2; it is `prunedAt` (rooms/_shared/0.2).
